name: Stepper-TS-TW
title: Stepper
description: A small dark panel with three numbered circles linked by bars, a title and paragraph for the current step, and Back and Continue buttons. Completed steps turn purple with a tick and the content slides sideways to the next step.
use: You split a signup or checkout into a few short screens and want the user to see where they are and how far is left.
avoid: Step circles are pointer-only and the dim helper text is hard to read on the dark panel.
a11y: Step circles are unfocusable divs, so keyboard users cannot jump steps, and step changes are not announced to screen readers. (keyboard: partial, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A narrow dark panel centred on a black stage. Across its top sit three small circles joined by thin grey bars: the active circle is purple with a dot, finished ones purple with a tick, upcoming ones grey with a number. Below are a bold white title, a dim grey paragraph, a small Back link and a green Continue pill.
behaves: Clicking Continue fills the connector, turns the indicator purple and slides the current content out as the next slides in, while the panel height eases to fit. Back reverses it, and on the last step the button reads Complete.
customise: Pass Step children and set the initial step, button labels, callbacks, and override class names or button props per part. Indicator colours, sizes and the slide motion are fixed in the source.
weight: light: A few motion elements and one spring height animation; nothing loops while idle.
